summary_md: **Cryptography and Security Papers ([@FSFG](https://x.com/FSFG/status/2115646583681266117))** shares **Blindfold**, a paper on keeping the audit "coin" secret from LLM agents so they cannot game audits.

referenced_urls.title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents

relevance: Unpredictable auditing as a defense against agents that adapt to oversight.

media.description: Abstract excerpt of Blindfold: audit-based certification of LLM agents also requires pre-commit noninterference (the audit coin must not leak into the agent's view), with worst-case bias (1-ε)D_A.
media.ocr_text: Audit-based certification bounds the violation rate of an LLM agent by auditing a random fraction ε of actions and reweighting the audited labels; its validity is meant to rest only on the defender's audit coin. We show that it also rests on a confidentiality property: the coin must not interfere with the agent's view before the action commits, at a time the agent chooses. We call this pre-commit noninterference (PNI) and measure its violation by D_A, the total-variation distance between the agent's views under the two coin values. PNI is necessary and sufficient for an unbiased certificate against adaptive agents, the worst-case bias is (1-ε)D_A, and no procedure that sees only audited labels can pay less. Leakage composes across steps, a resource shared across episodes opens a channel of computable size, and raising the audit rate cannot restore validity. On a monitor we built,…
